title: Inspect one word at two widths
audience: Students with basic programming knowledge who are new to assembly
learningObjectives: Interpret the same word as signed and unsigned
Relate binary and hexadecimal place values
Distinguish sign extension from zero extension
Explain word and doubleword arithmetic at a boundary
Verify full-width results independently of low-word formatting

quiz.prompt: Does switching from signed to unsigned interpretation change the stored word?

choices.text: Yes; the word grows automatically to eight bytes.
No; it changes the numerical interpretation of the same bits.

hints.text: State the width, bit pattern, interpretation, and observation boundary separately.
The same ffffffff pattern is signed -1 and unsigned 4294967295. Hex and binary describe the pattern directly.

steps.title: Store the other three full-width results

quiz.prompt: Why is a low-word-only check insufficient?

choices.text: A debugger automatically repairs the high half.
It cannot distinguish results whose upper 32 bits differ.
The low word never contains useful information.

hints.text: State the width, bit pattern, interpretation, and observation boundary separately.
For -1, unsigned_value has low bytes ff ff ff ff and high bytes 00 00 00 00. Both plus-one fields are zero.
